## 7. Data Quality Report

### 7.1 Zero-Income Rows

**2,008 rows** (2.0%) have zero total income.

These rows will produce extreme values in all income-ratio features (savings_rate, debt_to_income, essential_income_ratio).

![Zero Income Analysis](../figures/zero_income_analysis.png)

### 7.2 Outlier Summary (IQR Method)

| Feature | Outlier Count | Outlier % |
|---------|---------------|-----------|
| income_stability_cv | 6,290 | 6.2% |
| obligation_ratio | 2,222 | 2.2% |
| savings_rate | 3,018 | 3.0% |
| debt_to_income | 10,538 | 10.5% |
| discretionary_ratio | 2,159 | 2.1% |
| income_trend | 20,760 | 20.6% |
| expense_trend | 15,805 | 15.7% |
| volatility_index | 7,150 | 7.1% |

![Outlier Summary](../figures/outlier_summary.png)

### 7.3 Recommendations

1. **Zero-income rows (2.0%):** Expected behavior — intentional zero-income months from irregular/project-based income patterns. Not a bug.
2. **Skewed features:** Apply log or Box-Cox transformation to highly skewed features before linear models.
3. **Multicollinearity:** `obligation_ratio` and `essential_income_ratio` capture distinct constructs (obligation load vs essential share of income) and are currently weakly correlated (r≈0.06); monitor for divergence once obligatory expense fields (debt/loan repayments, remittances) are added.
4. **Month-1 degeneracy:** Early months have limited signal; consider excluding months 1-2 from training or adding minimum-history gates.
5. **Outlier capping:** The preprocessing pipeline already caps `debt_to_income` and `savings_rate` at 99th percentile; consider extending to other features.
